question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class expanded Control UI composer modal for long prompts, or should the existing inline auto-grow and send-shortcut behavior remain the supported composition model for now?
rationale: The current code can support a bounded implementation, but adding a new compose mode changes core Control UI UX and needs maintainer intent before automation should create a fix PR.

options.title: Sponsor expanded composer modal
options.body: Implement the requested modal editor in the Control UI composer with explicit draft, Apply, Cancel/Close, Send, focus, attachment, and keyboard tests.

options.title: Use inline composer only
options.body: Keep the current auto-growing inline composer and configurable send shortcut as the supported long-prompt workflow, then close this request with that product decision.

options.title: Narrow to another UX shape
options.body: Choose a smaller first step, such as larger auto-grow limits or a focused textarea mode, before committing to a modal workflow.

recommendation.title: Sponsor expanded composer modal
recommendation.body: Implement the requested modal editor in the Control UI composer with explicit draft, Apply, Cancel/Close, Send, focus, attachment, and keyboard tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this issue and owns adjacent recent composer shortcut work, making them the best available routing candidate for the product decision.
